To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the amount of precipitation in a given season (summer) can be recorded in the tooth enamel oxygen isotope values of Equus and, more clearly, Bison; (2) summer precipitation in the Chihuahuana Desert increased during the late glacial period, while summer precipitation in the Sonoran desert was minimal; and (3) the amount of summer precipitation can be inferred from the oxygen isotope values recorded in the tooth enamels of fossil Equus and Bison

oxygen isotopic data from the tooth enamel of fossil Equus and Bison provide a record of the amount and timing of summer rainfall in the Sonoran (Arizona) and Chihuahua (New Mexico) deserts during the Late Glacial period.
oxygen isotope data from serially sampled fossil teeth can be used to infer past amounts and seasonality of precipitation.
